### Part A - Basic Operations

```{r}
#A1. Create v as the sequence 5, 10, 15, ..., 50 using seq(). Print its length, sum and mean.

v <- seq(5, 50, by = 5)

v
length(v)
sum(v)
mean(v)
```

```{r}
#A2. Create w that repeats the vector c(1, 2, 3) four times and z that repeats each element of c(1, 2, 3) four times. Print both.

w <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), times = 4)
z <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), each = 4)

w
z
```

```{r}
#A3. Compute and print: the remainder of 17 divided by 5, the integer division of 17 by 5, 2 to the power of 10, the square root of 144, and pi rounded to 3 decimals.

17 %% 5
17 %/% 5
2 ^ 10
sqrt(144)
round(pi, 3)
```

```{r}
#A4.Given a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8) and b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7)

a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7)
a + b
a * b
a > b
sum(a * b)
```

```{r}
#A5. Use paste() to produce "Student-1, "Student-2, "Student-3". Then identify the datatype 42, 42L, 41i, and TRUE. What are its output?

paste("Student", 1:3, sep = "-")
```

### Part B: Data Frames and Conditional Statements
```{r}
#B1. Create a data frame students with 9 rowsand these columns (use stringsAsFactors = FALSE; sex is "M" or "F".

students <- data.frame(
  id = c(1:8),
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A","C","B","C","A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
students
```

```{r}
#B2. Display the structure, dimensions, column names, summary of students

str(students)
dim(students)
names(students)
summary(students)
```

```{r}
#B3. Add a column average = the mean of midterm and final for each student, rounded to 1 decimal

students$average <- round((students$midterm + students$final) / 2, 1)
students
```

```{r}
#B4. Add a logical column passed that is TRUE when average >= 70 and attendance >= 75

students$passed <- students$average >= 70 & students$attendance >= 75
students
```

```{r}
#B5. Using ifelse(), add a column standing with these values based on average.

students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors", ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))
students
```

```{r}
#B6. Write a function classify(score) that uses an if/else if/ else chain and returns "Distinction" for 85 and above, "Merit" for 70 to 84, "Pass" for 50 to 69, and "Fail" below 50. Test it with sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40))

classify <- function(score) {
  if(score >= 85) "Distinction"
  else if(score >= 70) "Merit"
  else if(score >= 50) "Pass"
  else "Fail"
}
sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)
```

### Part C: rbind() and cbind()
```{r}
#C1. Create a data frame new_students with two students. Its columns must match the original, including average, passed and standing, computed the same way: id 9, Ines, F, section C, midterm 81, final 84, attendance 92. id 10, Jamal, M, section A, midterm 70, final 68, attendance 80.
# Use rbind() to append them to students, saving the result as students_all

new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

new_students$average <- round((new_students$midterm + new_students$final) / 2, 1)

new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 70 & new_students$attendance >= 75

new_students$standing <- ifelse(new_students$average >= 90, "Honors", ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
students_all
```

```{r}
#C2. Create the numeric vector quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)

quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz = quiz)
students_all
class(students_all)
```

```{r}
#C3. Create the matrix m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final) and use rbind() to append a final row containing the column means, labelled "mean".

m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
m <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))
m
```

```{r}
#C4. In a comment (2-3 sentences), explain what error rbind() produces if the data frames have different column names and show the output if you safely catch it with tryCatch(). tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) { message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e));NULL }).

tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) { message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e));NULL })

# The error rbind() produces if the data frames have different column names is rbind failed: object '' not found and then it displays null safely instead of stopping the program completely if tryCatch() is used.
```

### Part D: Subsetting
```{r}
# Use students_all (with quiz) for all questions. Print every result.
#D1. Extract the name column in three ways: $, [["name"]], and [, "name"]

students_all$name
students_all[["name"]]
students_all[, "name"]
```

```{r}
#D2. Extract rows 2 to 5 and only the columns name, midterm, final.

students_all[2:5, c("name", "midterm", "final")]
```

```{r}
#D3. Using logical subsetting, select students with attendance above 90.

students_all[students_all$attendance > 90, ]
```

```{r}
#D4. Using subset(), select students of sex "F" in section "A" or "C" whose final is at least 75; return only name, section and final
subset(students_all, sex == "F" & section %in% c("A", "B") & final >= 75, select = c(name, section, final))
```

```{r}
#D5. Use which.max() and which.min() to report the name of the student with the highest and lowest average.

highest <- students_all$name[which.max(students_all$average)]
lowest <- students_all$name[which.min(students_all$average)]
highest
lowest
```

```{r}
#D6. Sort students_all by average in descending order, then print the top 3 rows.

sort <- students_all[order(students_all$average, decreasing = TRUE), ] 
head(sort, 3)
```

